The built-in service is shared by everyone using Lounge TV. If any minute, hourly or daily allowance is used up, TMDB details pause until that window resets; playlist information keeps working. Your own key or Worker removes this allowance.

Adds a record button to the player that saves the channel you are watching. It fetches the channel itself, so it uses one of your provider’s connections while it runs, and it keeps recording after you change channel or leave the player.

Recording fetches the channel a second time, so it uses another of your provider’s connections. On an account that allows only one, the recording is refused while you are watching. Once started it keeps going on its own — change channel, leave the player, and it carries on until the programme ends or you stop it from Recordings.
Carry on this long past the listed end time, so a programme that overruns is not cut off.
Begin this long before the listed start time, so a guide that runs a little early still catches the opening.
Keep one stream free for watching
Recordings leave one of your provider's connections free, so there is always one to watch on. Turn this off to record on every connection.
This device does not allow Lounge TV to set exact alarms, so a recording may begin a few minutes late. Recordings start earlier to make up for it.

The Lounge TV logo in the menu, About and setup shows its play triangle in your accent color. The icon on the home screen keeps its own colors.

Catch-up plays programs from your provider’s archive. Automatic uses the time zone your provider reports, or your TV’s own clock if it reports none; choose a fixed UTC offset if catch-up still starts at the wrong time. This is also where you choose which player catch-up uses.
Shows your provider’s channel number beside the name in the Live TV list, the channel-list overlay and the player, and lets you type a number on the remote in full screen to jump to that channel.
Looks on GitHub for a newer Lounge TV now and offers to install it. Your playlists, favorites and settings stay as they are.
Hide categories and items you never watch, give categories your own names and put them in your order. Hidden things come back here, never lost.
Looks up your provider’s addresses with a DNS server of your choice instead of your network’s own — useful when your network blocks or redirects them.
Add an XMLTV guide feed by its link, refresh it, or remove it. Feeds fill the TV Guide and the program lines in Live TV.
The ring drawn around whatever has focus. Pick its color and thickness so it stays easy to follow from the sofa.
The font used across Lounge TV, and how large text is drawn. Popups use the same font.
How many days of programs the guide stores ahead. Fewer days make guide refreshes faster and the database smaller.
Pick which rows Home shows and in what order, and how the Now trending row looks.
Uses the TV’s hardware decoder: smooth 4K and less heat. Turn it off only if some streams stutter or show blocks; the software decoder then does the work.

ExoPlayer opens channels much faster and is the only one with live subtitles. mpv plays channels ExoPlayer can’t, including some unusual audio. The combined options try the other player when the first one fails.
Stage shows the categories as a sheet that slides in with ◀, so the channel list and preview get the room. Separate keeps the categories on screen beside the list.
The focused channel plays in the preview beside the Live TV list, so you see what is on before you open it. Needs a layout with room for the preview.
The small player that keeps a channel going in a corner while you browse. Choose its size and the corner it sits in.

Floating: the menu rests as a small capsule over the content and slides open when you move left. Docked: it always takes its own room. Size sets how much it shows, from icons only to counts and details.
Add a playlist from a link, an Xtream login, a Stalker portal or a file, re-sync one, or remove it.
Makes popups, menus and dialogs larger or smaller as a whole. Use it when popups feel cramped or cover too much of the screen.
Plays the preview’s sound as well as its picture. Off keeps browsing quiet.
Ask to resume offers Resume or Start over when a film or episode has a saved position. Always resume carries on where you stopped; Never resume starts from the beginning.

What Lounge TV shows when it starts: Home, the channel you watched last, your favorites, or a channel you pick.
Subtitles in this language are switched on by themselves when a stream has them. Otherwise subtitles stay off until you pick a track in the player.
Dark is what Lounge TV is designed for. System follows the TV’s own setting where it has one; Light suits a bright room.
How far back Pause and rewind live TV can go on a channel without catch-up. Longer keeps more of the channel in this device’s storage.
Looks for a new version each time Lounge TV starts and tells you when there is one. Nothing is installed without asking.
Cinematic shows the focused title’s artwork behind a grid of posters. Separate shows categories, titles and details side by side.
The volume every channel, film and episode starts at. Above 100%% quiet streams are amplified. A volume you change in the player is kept for that title until you reset it.
Shows the temperature and your town next to the clock. Set a location by hand when the automatic one is wrong — behind a VPN, for example — and choose Celsius or Fahrenheit.
Scales everything on screen. Larger is easier to read from a distance; smaller fits more on screen. Below 85%% low-memory TV boxes can run out of memory.
How the picture fills the screen when playback starts. Fit shows the whole picture; the other choices fill, stretch or force a shape. A zoom changed in the player is kept for that title.

CH+ / CH− skip a page. Hold CH+ / CH− to jump to the last or first item.

Films only. When the TV has to re-sync to a new display mode, the film waits this long so its opening is not lost to the black screen. A seamless switch never pauses.

Films only. When the display mode changes for a film, the TV also switches to its resolution — 1080p for an HD film on a 4K TV — never above the resolution it started on. Off leaves the resolution alone and lets the TV upscale, usually the better picture.

On: Dolby and DTS go undecoded to the TV, soundbar or receiver when it says it can play them (ExoPlayer). Off: the app decodes them, still as surround where Surround sound allows. mpv always decodes. Not used while Night mode or Volume leveling is on.
Shift audio earlier or later to match the video. Works with both players (mpv and ExoPlayer).

Match the TV's refresh rate to the video (24/25/50/60 fps) in full screen, for Live TV and VOD, and restore it on exit. Turn off if your TV or receiver re-handshakes HDMI noisily on every channel change.
Not recommended on this TV: below Android 12 the rate can't be changed smoothly.
When an episode ends, automatically start the next one — and roll into the next season. Catch-up plays on to the next programme too.

Show your provider's channel number beside the name in the Live TV list, the channel-list overlay and the player — and type a number on the remote during full-screen playback to jump straight to that channel (OK tunes at once, Back cancels). Off hides every number and ignores the number keys; nothing is lost, and turning it back on restores them.
Volume applied when playback starts. Above 100%% quiet streams are amplified.

Keep a full trace of what the live engine does — every tune, fallback and reconnect — in Logcat and in the exported report. Leave it off unless you are chasing a problem; it never changes playback, only how much is written down.
Pick which sections open in an external app.

Open streams in an external app (VLC, MX Player) instead of the built-in player, chosen per section. Useful for streams this app can't decode, or if you prefer another player. Resume position and prev/next are unavailable while playing externally; streams needing a custom User-Agent or referer may not play.

On: ExoPlayer can also decode sound your device has no decoder for, such as DTS, TrueHD or MP2. The device's own decoders still come first. Off: ExoPlayer uses only the device's decoders. mpv always decodes with FFmpeg. Changing this restarts OwnTV.
The audio decoder changes after OwnTV restarts.
Use the TV's hardware decoder. Turn off if some streams stutter or show artifacts.
Override the setting above for one playlist, for a provider whose channels only one of the players handles well.
On a very high-bitrate channel — 4K especially — the buffer may hold less time than you asked for, because there is a limit on how much video can be kept in memory at once.
How close to the live broadcast to play. Lower means closer to live but a smaller buffer, so weak streams may stutter or reconnect more. Applies to the next channel you open.
